Sources: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001628280-26-004357, filed January 30, 2026) and the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-26-096787, filed March 6, 2026; principal shareholders as of the dates in its footnotes, share count at December 31, 2025). LEADER: David Calhoun ceased to be CEO on August 8, 2024 and retired from Boeing on March 1, 2025 (per the 2025 proxy, read for the prior edition). The 2026 proxy names him only as the prior CEO in the pay-versus-performance table; he is not a director or named executive officer and is not in its ownership tables, so status is no-reported-stake. 5% HOLDERS: Vanguard and FMR report holdings as of December 31, 2025; BlackRock's 6.8% rests on a filing as of December 31, 2024 and is stale. DIVIDENDS: no common dividends were paid in 2025 (suspended since 2020). The cash-flow statement shows $331 million of "Dividends paid on Mandatory convertible preferred stock" in 2025; that is a separate line for preferred holders, so it is excluded and dividends are recorded as 0. BUYBACKS: the quoted Item 5 footnote covers the fourth quarter; for the full year the cash-flow statement has no share repurchase line, and its $34 million "Employee taxes on certain share-based payment arrangements" is tax withholding, not a buyback. STOCK COMP: $426 million is the cash-flow add-back. GEOGRAPHY: the eight regional rows sum to the reported $89,463 million total; the 737 MAX concessions reconciling line has no 2025 amount.

Supplier spend by state: Boeing's per-state 'state cards' (boeing.com/.../state_cards/Card_XX.pdf) returned 404 for every state in the earlier research (not rechecked in this refresh), and the U.S. page gives only national figures, so no state supplier-spend rows are recorded. Sites: corporate HQ from the FY2025 10-K cover; the eight state 'key sites' cards from Boeing's U.S. page (still live, checked 2026-11-24) are state-level descriptions, not single facilities. The 10-K's Item 2 lists major locations (e.g. Greater Seattle, Wichita, Greater Charleston, Greater St. Louis) without figures.
